bullets.title: NVDA: MS reinstates Top Pick ($300 PT); $150B buyback added; Feynman targets $60B/GW
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley reinstated NVDA as Top Pick with a $300 PT (~20x CY27 EPS) after NDR meetings confirmed diverse customer base, Vera Rubin product cycle in early stage, and Feynman (2028) expected to drive revenue per GW from $40B to >$50B. Separately, NVDA added $150B to its buyback authorization (total $235B through FY28). Agentic AI driving 10x incremental inference tokens vs human users; LPS constraints favor NVDA efficiency over ASICs. Multiple sources corroborate 72-73% GM as FY28 floor.

bullets.title: MU: Massive beat-and-raise; >75% of CY27 output committed; buybacks start Dec 9
bullets.body: Micron reported F4Q revenue $54.23B (+5.7% above consensus), EPS $33.42, with F1Q guidance of $61.5B revenue and $38.15 EPS both ~7% above Street. Management expects supply-demand to be 'much tighter in CY27/28 than 2026'; 26 long-term supply agreements cover >35% of revenue through 2030; >75% of CY27 output already committed with HBM pricing materially higher. Company targeting 100% excess cash returns via buybacks starting Dec 9, 2026. Multiple analysts raised PTs: UBS $1,625, Raymond James $1,500, DA Davidson raised to Buy.

bullets.title: ACN: F4Q smash beat (+17% stock); FY27 guide 3-6% beats Street; bookings inflect positive
bullets.body: Accenture reported F4Q revenue $18.68B (beat $18.03B consensus), EPS $3.29 vs $3.18, with bookings of $22.2B (+5% y/y CC). FY27 guidance of +3-6% CC revenue growth beats prior Street expectation of +1-4%. Bookings inflected from -3% in F3Q to +5% in F4Q. RBC raises PT to $240 (16x FY27 EPS); Mizuho Outperform $226 PT; JPMorgan positive. AI bookings 3x, revenue 2x vs 2025. FY27 EPS guidance $14.39-14.81; FCF $11.0-11.8B with $9.5B+ returns planned.

bullets.title: WDC/STX: Down 8-13% on Toshiba HDD expansion; Citi says buy the dip ($740/$1300 PTs)
bullets.body: Toshiba plans to invest ¥60B ($380M) to roughly double HDD production capacity by FY27, targeting 30% market share from ~10%. WDC fell ~8-14% and STX fell ~11% on the news. Citi maintains Buy on both—STX $1,300 PT and WDC $740 PT (both 23x FY28 EPS)—arguing Toshiba lacks internal media/heads supply, limiting EB impact, and that supply-demand gap remains >300 EB with capacity sold through CY28. MS also recommends buying the dip; VECO highlighted as equipment play.

bullets.title: LITE/COHR: FCC optical transceiver restrictions on China at 3.2T generation seen as major tailwind
bullets.body: Multiple banks (MS, JPM, Wolfe) flagged that likely FCC restrictions on Chinese-built optical transceivers—phased in at the 3.2T generation (~2028 ramp)—would benefit US laser vendors LITE and COHR. LITE rallied 7.7% and COHR +10.9% on the week. MS argues laser pricing and US content requirements (65% BOM workaround) are the key read-through. Jefferies sees AI transceiver demand accelerating to 180M units in C27 and 245M in C28. Roth QSG surveying GPU cluster optics sourcing to quantify switching.

bullets.title: META: Enterprise Platform launched; Muse hits 3M weekly users in <30 days; Top Pick at MS/Hedgeye
bullets.body: META launched its Enterprise Platform (Muse agent, Business Agent, Muse API, Muse Code) and simultaneously hired MongoDB CEO CJ Desai as Chief Enterprise Platform Officer. META Muse surpassed 3M weekly users and 5M downloads in ~22 days post-launch, faster than ChatGPT/Grok/Claude. MS and Hedgeye both name META as top large-cap alpha pick; MS bull case $775 PT noting CPU capacity for 1B Muse DAUs already in $209B FY27 opex model. Muse for Small Business launched connecting to Asana, Zoom, Intuit, Box, Canva, Slack.

bullets.title: GOOGL: Gemini 4 Argon launched; Citi reiterates Buy $447 PT; JPM raises PT to $420 on TPU monetization
bullets.body: Google released Gemini 4 Argon, ranking top in 14 of 19 benchmarks vs GPT-6 Astra and Claude Fable 5.1, with 1M-token output limit and pricing at $2-4/1M tokens (vs $10-50 for rivals). Citi reiterates Buy $447 PT calling it a 'key overhang removal.' JPM raises Dec-27 PT to $420 on TPU monetization ($4-7B in 2026, $30B+ in 2027) and Cloud accelerating to +88% in 3Q. Antitrust suits from Chegg/Penske dismissed. Internal employee skepticism on real-world performance noted.

bullets.title: MDB: CEO CJ Desai departs to META; stock -18-25%; Dev Ittycheria returns as interim CEO
bullets.body: MongoDB CEO Chirantan Desai resigned effective immediately to join META as Chief Enterprise Platform Officer, less than one year after joining. Dev Ittycheria (CEO 2014-2025) returned as interim CEO; board initiating permanent search. FY27 guidance reaffirmed; Investor Day held Sept 29 as planned. Wolfe maintains Outperform $500 PT calling departure opportunity-driven; Hedgeye flagged it as net negative for enterprise AI go-to-market. DA Davidson, DA Davidson, and others maintain Buy despite the leadership change.

bullets.title: AVGO: $42B lend to Anthropic; NDR bullish on F2027/F2028 AI revenue doubling YoY; UBS $470 PT
bullets.body: Broadcom agreed to lend Anthropic up to $42B for infrastructure purchases (convertible into Anthropic common stock). UBS NDR recap: AVGO confirmed 4-5GW/yr TPU shipments in C2027, XPU roadmap scaling from 4 to 8 and 16 dies; AI networking ~30% of AI revenue; 40-45% FCF margins; could repay all debt by end of 2027. F2027 AI revenue to at least double YoY, F2028 to double again—guidance viewed as conservative. PT $470 (17x Software FCF + 30x Semis FCF on CY27E).

bullets.title: HPE: Daiwa upgrades to Outperform ($75 PT); Networking Day raises FY27 growth to high-teens/low-20%
bullets.body: Daiwa upgraded HPE to Outperform from Neutral, raising PT to $75 from $65. HPE's Networking Investor Day raised FY27 Networking revenue growth to high-teens to low-20% (from +8-12%), increased Juniper synergies to $800M by FY28 (from $600M+), and announced $1.2B Vultr AMD Helios AI Rack order. DC Networking CAGR low-to-high 50s% through FY29. MS raises PT to $72 (EPS 11-13% above Street at $5.10/$5.76 FY27/28). Stock hit 52-week high (+174% YTD).

bullets.title: SHOP: MS and JPM bullish as Agentic commerce winner; Muse/Canvas launch; payments upside
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley highlighted SHOP as 'agnostic Agentic shopping winner' given transaction-based monetization model—Canvas AI store-builder tool launched. Payments penetration reached ~70% GMV with Shopify Payments at 68%; new 1.25% premium fee for third-party processor users adds upside. Shop Pay integrated into Meta Muse and Instinct AI agents. Nationwide money transmitter license pursuit could add ~2% GP and 5% EBIT by 2028. UBS maintains Neutral noting limited upside near-term but acknowledges payment penetration upside.

bullets.title: MRVL: Investor Day (Oct 6) expected to raise 2030 targets to $40B+ revenue, $15-20 EPS
bullets.body: Multiple banks previewing MRVL's Oct 6 Investor Day: Piper sees $45B revenue and ~$19 EPS power (45% CAGR) with 'XPU Attach' opportunity underestimated; Citi expects $15-20 2030 EPS on 40%+ AI infrastructure CAGR and raised FY27/FY28 revenue to $12B/$18B; Jefferies bullish on OmniConnect ramp with Positron AI offering $1B+ opportunity. Google v9 TPU potentially shifting to MRVL from MediaTek after MTK delays. Piper's tactical positive heading into event.

bullets.title: DKNG: Prediction markets pulling forward spend; short bias at Hedgeye; FLUT moves to Long Bias
bullets.body: DKNG's DKeX prediction market exchange grew 22x MoM in September to ~$2B in contracts (2.8% market share); monthly combo volume projected $350-420M by year-end. However, DKNG is pulling forward prediction market investment from FY27 into FY26—total PM spend expected to exceed prior $200-300M guidance, risking miss on $700-900M FY26 adj. EBITDA guide. Hedgeye keeps DKNG on Short Bias into Q4 2027. Hedgeye moved FLUT to Long Bias. 6th Circuit ruling adds regulatory headwinds to sports prediction markets.

bullets.title: AAPL: iPhone Duo assembly yields ~60%, Vision Pro delayed to 2029; smart-home push Oct 13
bullets.body: Apple's iPhone Duo showing ~60% final assembly yields in mid-September, normalizing over 6-12 months and limiting supply. Vision Pro team on 'life support' with product pushed to late 2028/early 2029. New CEO reorganization creating execution risk with faster development cycles. October 13 Apple event expected to unveil J490 smart-home hub, updated HomePod mini, and new TV set-top box (manufactured in Vietnam with BYD). Hedgeye/MS both bullish on AAPL in large-cap tech; MS sees FY27 EPS ~$10, stock at 35x CY27 P/E viewed as 'full.'

bullets.title: MSFT: Cloud ROIC stabilizing at 32-33%; Copilot Super App >30M paid subs; JPM OW $625 PT
bullets.body: JPM reiterates OW on MSFT ($625 PT), estimating Microsoft Cloud ROIC at ~37% in FY26 declining to ~32-33% FY27-31E as capex scales—still second-highest among hyperscalers. Copilot has exceeded 30M paid subscribers (faster than prior MSFT products). JPM webinar with TD SYNNEX planned Oct 6 on Copilot/M365 distribution. Piper raises PT to $610 on M365 consumption revenue path to $2B run-rate by FY28. Hedgeye names MSFT as 'alpha dog' mega-cap alongside META.

bullets.title: GLW: AT&T signs $3B+ multi-year fiber supply deal; MS maintains Equal-Weight $165 PT
bullets.body: AT&T signed a multi-year fiber and cable supply agreement with Corning valued at more than $3B. Corning also has Verizon secured for 80M+ fiber miles through 2032 and an NVDA-backed route expansion through 2030. MS maintains Equal-Weight, noting incremental margins will cycle through two below-average and two above-average quarters as capacity ramps. GLW Display faces pressure from elevated memory costs (~3x higher in 3Q) limiting TV maker 2027 commitments. Enterprise segment up 65% y/y on Meta, Amazon, NVDA demand.

bullets.title: CCL: Strong 3Q beat; 2027 bookings at record occupancy/pricing; UBS Buy $36 PT
bullets.body: Carnival reported 3Q Adjusted EBITDA $2.99B (beat $2.88B guide), EPS $1.43 (beat $1.35). FY26 net yield raised to +2.3% CC (from +1.75%); FY26 adj. EPS raised to $2.24. 2027 already ~50% booked at record occupancy and pricing; 2028 tracking ahead. Customer deposits hit Q3 record of $7.6B (+7% YoY despite flat capacity). S&P upgraded CCL to investment grade. RCL and Citi both turn more bullish; Middle East fears waning on accelerating 3Q bookings.

bullets.title: PSKY/WBD: Merger closes Oct 6; ticker changes to SKYD; Mattel CEO Kreiz joins combined entity
bullets.body: Paramount-Warner Bros. merger received judicial approval and is set to close October 6, with PSKY changing ticker to SKYD and Class B shares listing on NYSE. Combined entity projects $6B in synergies but faces net leverage >4x at peak rate environment. Ynon Kreiz (Mattel CEO) announced as senior leader at the combined company. Wells Fargo sees streaming super-app as biggest long-term opportunity. MS notes media sector sold off ~-10% for PSKY on rate headwinds and fund rotation.

bullets.title: HOOD: MS upgrades to OW ($150 PT); Sept volumes strong; Robinhood Agents launched at Summit
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley upgraded HOOD to Overweight with $150 PT on broader platform, deeper wallet share, and stronger durable growth. HOOD Summit unveiled ~15 platform updates: agentic trading experience, earnings prediction market contracts, perpetual futures via Bitstamp. 150K+ customers already using agentic accounts. KeyBanc raises PT to $140 (OW) on new products. GS upgraded with PT to $145 on September crypto/prediction-market volume (+21%/+17% MoM). Goldman adds to conviction on prediction markets super-cycle.

bullets.title: NFLX: Co-CEO acknowledges slower-than-desired growth; Deutsche Bank upgrades to Buy ($95 PT)
bullets.body: Netflix co-CEO Ted Sarandos stated the company is 'not growing as fast as I want us to' and cited engagement only +2% despite double-digit revenue growth across regions. Company allocating ~5% of $20B content budget to live programming. Deutsche Bank upgraded NFLX to Buy from Hold, cutting PT to $95 from $100 citing valuation. Hedgeye and MS risk range both flag NFLX as bearish near-term at $67-73 range. David Fincher ended 13-year exclusive Netflix deal, joining broader talent departures.
